question: When welding high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steel, which preheat consideration is most critical to prevent hydrogen-induced cracking?
options: Maintaining interpass temperature below 50°C
Calculating preheat based on carbon equivalent (CE) formula
Using only DCEP polarity regardless of process
Applying post-weld heat treatment before removing clamps

question: A welder is performing a Charpy V-notch impact test on a weld sample. What property of the weld metal does this test primarily evaluate?
options: Tensile strength at elevated temperatures
Toughness and resistance to brittle fracture
Hardness across the heat-affected zone
Fatigue life under cyclic loading

question: In GTAW (TIG) welding of austenitic stainless steel, which shielding gas mixture provides the best arc stability and weld quality while avoiding sensitization?
options: Argon with 2% oxygen
Argon with 75% helium
100% nitrogen

question: Which discontinuity is most likely detected by radiographic testing (RT) but would be missed by dye penetrant testing (PT)?
options: Surface porosity
Lack of fusion at the root
Undercutting along the weld toe
Surface cracks in the heat-affected zone

question: When fabricating a pressure vessel in accordance with ASME Section VIII, what is the primary purpose of the post-weld heat treatment (PWHT)?
options: To increase the hardness of the weld metal
To relieve residual stresses and reduce susceptibility to stress corrosion cracking
To improve the visual appearance of the weld bead
To increase tensile strength beyond the base metal

question: A flux-cored arc welding (FCAW) procedure requires an E71T-1C electrode. What does the designation '1C' signify?
options: Single-pass only weld with DCEN polarity
All-position capability with CO2 shielding gas
Flat and horizontal position with mixed gas shielding
Vertical-down progression with argon shielding

question: During submerged arc welding (SAW), what is the main function of the flux in relation to the arc and weld pool?
options: It acts as a filler material replacing the electrode wire
It shields the arc, provides alloying elements, and forms a protective slag over the molten pool
It generates shielding gas to prevent atmospheric contamination only
It controls amperage by varying electrical resistance

question: In structural steel fabrication, which welding symbol annotation on a drawing indicates that the weld is to be made in the field rather than in the shop?
options: A contour finish symbol above the reference line
A filled circle at the junction of the reference line and arrow
A tail with a specification note
An all-around symbol on the reference line

question: When performing ultrasonic testing (UT) on a weld, a technician uses a 70° angle beam transducer. What type of internal discontinuity is this angle best suited to detect?
options: Laminations parallel to the plate surface
Vertical planar discontinuities such as cracks and lack of fusion
Surface porosity open to the weld face
Compositional segregation in the base metal

question: Which metallurgical phenomenon occurs in the heat-affected zone (HAZ) of austenitic stainless steel welded without adequate controls, leading to intergranular corrosion?
options: Martensite transformation
Sensitization due to chromium carbide precipitation at grain boundaries
Sigma phase embrittlement at low temperatures
Hydrogen embrittlement from dissolved hydrogen

question: A fabricator must join a 25 mm thick carbon steel plate using SMAW. According to AWS D1.1, which joint design would typically require a full penetration groove weld verified by non-destructive examination?
options: A fillet weld in the flat position
A complete joint penetration (CJP) butt weld in a primary structural tension member
A partial joint penetration groove weld under compressive loading
A lap joint with intermittent fillet welds

question: In plasma arc cutting (PAC), what is the role of the secondary (shield) gas surrounding the plasma stream?
options: It initiates the pilot arc between electrode and nozzle
It constricts the plasma and protects the cut surface from oxidation
It cools the work piece to prevent distortion
It provides additional electrical conductivity to the arc

question: When evaluating weld distortion in a fabricated T-joint assembly, which technique is most effective for controlling angular distortion before welding begins?
options: Increasing travel speed significantly
Pre-setting or pre-cambering the joint at an angle opposite to expected distortion
Applying a higher heat input to slow the cooling rate
Using DCEN polarity to reduce penetration

question: Which destructive test method is used to assess the ductility of a weld and its heat-affected zone by bending the specimen through a specified angle over a mandrel?
options: Macro examination test
Guided bend test
Nick break test
Vickers hardness test

question: When welding duplex stainless steel (e.g., 2205), what is the most critical parameter to control to maintain the correct austenite-to-ferrite phase balance in the weld metal?
options: Shielding gas dew point below −40°C
Heat input and interpass temperature within the procedure-specified range
Use of DCEN polarity only
Post-weld pickling and passivation immediately after welding
